beats.text: Right now, as ChatGPT writes its answer to you, it has no idea how its own sentence is going to end.
beats.dir: clear, engaging explainer tone, natural pace
beats.chapter: No plan, one word at a time

beats.text: It doesn't plan the paragraph. It doesn't even plan the next sentence. It picks one small piece of a word, then the next, then the next.
beats.dir: clear, engaging explainer tone, natural pace

beats.text: And yet about a billion people use it every week, to write emails, fix code and explain homework.
beats.dir: clear, engaging explainer tone, natural pace

beats.text: So how can something that is basically guessing, one word at a time, sound so smart? Let's open the box.
beats.dir: clear, engaging explainer tone, natural pace

beats.text: First, ChatGPT doesn't actually read words. It reads tokens.
beats.dir: clear, engaging explainer tone, natural pace

beats.text: A token is a chunk of text. Sometimes a whole word, sometimes just a piece of one. On average, a hundred tokens make about seventy-five English words.
beats.dir: clear, engaging explainer tone, natural pace
